{"id": "c8715ae0-540d-422f-baec-d45116373a5c", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_tDLHgAUivwuMDpD25pXD56", "content": [{"text": "{"iso8601":"2026-09-28T19:35:31.599200+00:00","unix":1790624131.599,"day_of_week":"Monday"}"}], "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_wQKn2eTbbPXCUn1Mocz8v1", "content": [{"text": "     1	---
     2	name: aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation
     3	description: Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or
     4	  EKS), ParallelCluster, or self-managed EC2/EKS GPU instances. It adds three things.
     5	  First, a GPU evidence coverage audit that proves per node whether kernel Xid logs and
     6	  HyperPod health-agent detections were actually arriving, hour by hour, so "no errors
     7	  found" is never reported from a silent log. Second, a node verdict (replace, reboot,
     8	  or leave alone) against an explicit evidence bar, so an application Xid is never
     9	  headlined as hardware. Third, a pre-flight readiness check before a long run, covering
     10	  Capacity Block or training plan end time versus run length, spare capacity to replace
     11	  a failed node, NodeRecovery, deep health checks, EFA, log coverage, idle reserved
     12	  GPUs. Activate on Xid or ECC errors, slow training or FSx for Lustre slowness on a GPU
     13	  cluster, NCCL hangs or TCP fallback, NVLink or Fabric Manager errors, nodes in Failure
     14	  or Pending, nodes terminating at once, or "is my cluster ready for a multi-day run".
     15	metadata:
     16	  author: nzuresh
     17	  version: "1.0.0"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA, Chat tasks"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, AWS ParallelCluster, Amazon EC2, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Elastic Fabric Adapter, Amazon EKS, AWS Health"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Machine Learning, GenAI, High Performance Computing"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass.** In chat, do not stop to ask a question and do not hand off to a
     34	   separate investigation before answering. If an input is missing, use the default (impact
     35	   window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and 72 hours), state the assumption,
     36	   and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or performance questions with no
     37	   time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only after the answer.
     38	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     39	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     40	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     41	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     42	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     43	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     44	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     45	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     46	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     47	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     48	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     49	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     50	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     51	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     52	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     53	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     54	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     55	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     56	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.
     57	R4. **Find every log source by substring, not prefix.** Call `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with
     58	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for
     59	   `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`, `journal`, and `gpu`, paginating with `nextToken`. Never
     60	   search only `/aws/parallelcluster` or `/aws/sagemaker` prefixes: customer pipelines use
     61	   other names (for example `/aws/<pipeline>/<cluster>/kernel`). Evaluate every source found.
     62	R5. **Prove coverage before any "no errors".** For each node and source: find the stream that
     63	   carries `kernel:` lines, then bin **that exact stream** by hour across the window padded by
     64	   one hour. **Always name the evidence you used: quote the full log group name and the exact
     65	   log stream name for every node in the coverage table, and again in the answer text.** A
     66	   coverage claim without the group and stream it rests on is not auditable, so the operator
     67	   cannot re-run it. Any empty hour means `Not observable` for that hour. First and last event times
     68	   are not proof, and the time of the **last `kernel:` line** is not when logging stopped:
     69	   a healthy kernel goes quiet. Liveness comes only from the hourly bins of all lines in
     70	   that stream. A node is `Measured` if one source passes. HyperPod: a missing
     71	   `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<group>/<instance-id>` stream means `No HMA detections`
     72	   when the cluster log group is otherwise live. NCCL transport with no `NCCL INFO` lines
     73	   anywhere is `Not observable`; never infer it from the instance type.
     74	R6. **Verdict per node, headline to match.** `REPLACE`, `REBOOT`, `LEAVE ALONE`, `MONITOR`, or
     75	   `NOT OBSERVABLE`, against the evidence bar in `references/incident-branches.md` (Step 4b).
     76	   Application-class Xids (for example 13, 31) or HMA `reason: XidUserAppError` with the node
     77	   `Running` is `LEAVE ALONE`. Never headline "hardware error" unless the verdict is `REPLACE`
     78	   or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds.
     79	R7. **Label every cause** `Proven` (measured signal on the affected node, before the failure,
     80	   nothing competing) or `Hypothesis (to validate)` with the one confirming measurement. A
     81	   spike at the same time is correlation. FSx without a saturated metric is not a proven cause.
     82	   Only a `Proven` cause may be called the root cause, in the headline or in a branch table.
     83	   Otherwise write `Leading hypothesis: <cause>`, or `Root cause: Not observable` when the
     84	   deciding evidence is missing (for example a dead control-plane log). Never write "Proven
     85	   mechanism" for something whose trigger or removal path you did not observe.
     86	   Utilization metrics from FSx (`NetworkThroughputUtilization`, `DiskIopsUtilization`, and
     87	   similar) and `GPUPowerUtilization` are already percent from 0 to 100: a value of `0.9` is
     88	   0.9 percent. Quote the raw value with a percent sign.
     89	R8. **Recovery questions** always state three things: whether automatic node recovery is on
     90	   (`NodeRecovery`), what it does (reboot or replace the node), and that the **job** resumes
     91	   only with checkpoints plus the orchestrator's auto-resume (Slurm on HyperPod:
     92	   `srun --auto-resume=1`).
     93	R9. **Capacity Blocks** begin terminating instances 30 minutes before the end time (60 for
     94	   UltraServers); blocks end at 11:30 UTC and termination starts at 11:00 UTC on the last day.
     95	   For a planned run, write out: usable until = end time minus the lead time; run end = start
     96	   plus run length; hours covered = usable until minus start. Give every value as a full UTC
     97	   date and time, and check the latest safe start is not already in the past.
     98	R10. **Rule out the frequent non-GPU causes** in `references/cluster-edge-cases.md` before
     99	   blaming hardware: subnet IP or network interface exhaustion, ParallelCluster bootstrap
     100	   failures and protected mode, EFA nodes in a public subnet, a Capacity Block not yet
     101	   active, and the FSx maintenance window. HyperPod does not export system metrics to
     102	   CloudWatch, so HyperPod GPU activity is `Not observable` there.
     103	
     104	## Pick the mode
     105	
     106	| The user asks | Mode | Steps to run |
     107	|---------------|------|--------------|
     108	| Something failed, hung, slowed, or lost nodes | **I: Incident** | Steps 1 to 7 |
     109	| "Were there GPU errors?", "Can I trust the logs?" | **C: Coverage audit** | Steps 1 to 3, then 6 and 7 |
     110	| "Is the cluster ready for a long run?", Capacity Block ending | **P: Pre-flight** | Steps 1 to 3, then 5P, 6 and 7 |
     111	
     112	## Workflow checklist
     113	
     114	Work through these in order and tick each one as it completes. Skip only the steps the
     115	mode table excludes. Every step below has a matching `## Step N` section with its detail.
     116	
     117	- [ ] Step 1: Scope the request — account, region, cluster or instance IDs, impact window
     118	- [ ] Step 2: Build the inventory, capability profile, and one ordered timeline
     119	- [ ] Step 3: Prove GPU log coverage per node before looking for errors
     120	- [ ] Step 4: Classify each fault and give every node a verdict
     121	- [ ] Step 5: Pull metrics and settle the root-cause branch
     122	- [ ] Step 5P: Score pre-flight checks P1 to P16 (Mode P only, replaces Steps 4 and 5)
     123	- [ ] Step 6: Write the report in the required format
     124	- [ ] Step 7: Self-check the finished output, then present it
     125	
     126	## Step 1: Scope
     127	
     128	Account, region, cluster name or instance IDs, workload, impact window (default last 24 hours,
     129	stated). Classify the symptom to pick a starting branch (Step 5), but collect evidence for all.
     130	
     131	## Step 2: Inventory and timeline
     132	
     133	Load [references/inventory-and-timeline.md](references/inventory-and-timeline.md) for the
     134	inventory API calls and the seven timeline sources, and
     135	[references/cluster-edge-cases.md](references/cluster-edge-cases.md) for the frequent non-GPU
     136	causes to rule out under rule R10:
     137	
     138	```
     139	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/inventory-and-timeline.md")
     140	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/cluster-edge-cases.md")
     141	```
     142	
     143	Build one ordered timeline for the window plus 30 minutes each side: node state, HMA
     144	detections, Xids, AWS Health, EC2 status and scheduled events, Capacity Block and training plan
     145	end times, and CloudTrail cluster changes (rule R3).
     146	
     147	## Step 3: Coverage audit
     148	
     149	Load [references/coverage-audit.md](references/coverage-audit.md) for the log-source discovery
     150	and hourly coverage queries, and
     151	[references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md](references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md) for NCCL transport, NVLink and
     152	NVSwitch, and EFA signals:
     153	
     154	```
     155	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/coverage-audit.md")
     156	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md")
     157	```
     158	
     159	Produce the coverage table and the node capability and fabric table for every affected node.
     160	Every row names the full log group name and the exact log stream name that row's verdict rests
     161	on, so the operator can re-run the same query. Where no stream carries kernel lines, say which
     162	groups you searched and that none did.
     163	
     164	## Step 4: Classify faults and give node verdicts
     165	
     166	Load [references/xid-triage.md](references/xid-triage.md) for the Xid catalog and per-code
     167	verdicts, and [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) for the node
     168	verdict evidence bar and branches A to F:
     169	
     170	```
     171	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/xid-triage.md")
     172	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/incident-branches.md")
     173	```
     174	
     175	## Step 5: Metrics and root-cause branch
     176	
     177	Load [references/signals-and-thresholds.md](references/signals-and-thresholds.md) for metric
     178	names, dimensions, and thresholds:
     179	
     180	```
     181	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/signals-and-thresholds.md")
     182	```
     183	
     184	Pull FSx (correct dimensions per metric), GPU activity (`AWS/EC2` `GPUPowerUtilization`, unit
     185	Percent, or `CWAgent`), and EFA counters, then evaluate branches A (hardware), B (capacity
     186	lifecycle), C (storage), D (NCCL, NVLink/NVSwitch, EFA), E (cluster change), and F (application,
     187	only after A to E are ruled out), as defined in `incident-branches.md`. Recommend operator
     188	actions only.
     189	
     190	## Step 5P: Pre-flight readiness (Mode P)
     191	
     192	Load [references/preflight.md](references/preflight.md) for pre-flight checks P1 to P16:
     193	
     194	```
     195	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/preflight.md")
     196	```
     197	
     198	Score checks P1 to P16. Lead with FAIL, then RISK. In Mode P this step replaces
     199	Steps 4 and 5.
     200	
     201	## Step 6: Report
     202	
     203	Load [references/report-format.md](references/report-format.md) for the report template and its rules:
     204	
     205	```
     206	read_skill_resource(skill_id="aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation", path="references/report-format.md")
     207	```
     208	
     209	## Step 7: Self-check before presenting
     210	
     211	Before showing the answer to the user, re-read your own draft and verify each of these.
     212	Fix the draft where a check fails; do not present an output that fails one.
     213	
     214	- [ ] Every "no errors found" statement is backed by a node whose coverage you proved in
     215	      Step 3. If coverage was not proven, the wording is `Not observable`, not healthy.
     216	- [ ] Every coverage row names its full log group and exact log stream (rule R5). A coverage
     217	      claim with no named source is not auditable and must be fixed before presenting.
     218	- [ ] Every node verdict still meets the evidence bar that justifies it, re-read from
     219	      [references/incident-branches.md](references/incident-branches.md) Step 4b.
     220	- [ ] The headline matches the verdicts. It does not say "hardware error" unless a verdict
     221	      is `REPLACE` or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds (rule R6).
     222	- [ ] Every cause carries a `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)` label, and anything
     223	      labelled `Proven` has a measured signal on the affected node before the failure
     224	      (rule R7). Nothing unproven is called the root cause.
     225	- [ ] Every percentage came straight from the metric without rescaling (rule R7).
     226	- [ ] Every absent signal is reported as `Not observable` with what to collect, never as
     227	      zero or as healthy.
     228	- [ ] Each recommendation names an operator action, and no mutating API call was made.
     229	- [ ] Every number in the answer can be traced to a call you actually made this run.
     230	
     231	State the outcome of this self-check in one line, naming anything you could not verify.
     232	
     233	## Success criteria
     234	
     235	- Coverage table and node capability table for every affected node; no "no errors" without
     236	  proven coverage.
     237	- One verdict per node with a GPU signal; headline consistent with the verdicts.
     238	- Every cause labelled `Proven` or `Hypothesis (to validate)`.
     239	- Replaced nodes matched to the operator or automatic action that replaced them.
     240	- Mode P: P1 to P16 scored.
     241	- No mutating API call was made.
     242

     246	- [HyperPod deep health checks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-hyperpod-resiliency-slurm-deep-health-checks.html)
     247	- [Manually replace or reboot a HyperPod node](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-hyperpod-resiliency-slurm-replace-faulty-instance.html)
     248	- [HyperPod Slurm cluster logging](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-hyperpod-cluster-management-slurm.html)
     249	- [ClusterInstanceStatusDetails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_ClusterInstanceStatusDetails.html)
     250	- [How Capacity Blocks work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/capacity-blocks-how.html)
     251	- [EFA security group requirements](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/efa-start-nccl.html)
     252	- [Monitor Capacity Blocks using EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/capacity-blocks-monitor.html)
     253	- [FSx for Lustre metrics and dimensions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/fs-metrics.html)
     254	- [NVIDIA Xid catalog](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/xid-errors/analyzing-xid-catalog.html)
     255	- [EC2 accelerator metrics (GPUPowerUtilization)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/viewing_metrics_with_cloudwatch.html#accelerator-metrics)
     256	- [DescribeTrainingPlan](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_DescribeTrainingPlan.html)

{"id": "15f7bcf3-8bc2-4003-88d7-9af009d3037d", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_4Aqho9eAmIxUYFNsFs8KO5", "content": [{"text": "     1	# Signals and Thresholds
     2	
     3	Thresholds here are investigation heuristics for flagging a signal as worth reporting.
     4	They are not AWS service limits. State the observed value, not only the label.
     5	
     6	## HyperPod node state
     7	
     8	Valid `InstanceStatus.Status` values
     9	([ClusterInstanceStatusDetails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_ClusterInstanceStatusDetails.html)):
     10	`Running | Failure | Pending | ShuttingDown | SystemUpdating | DeepHealthCheckInProgress | NotFound`.
     11	
     12	| Signal | Flag when |
     13	|--------|-----------|
     14	| Node in `Failure` | Always. Correlate with HMA log for that instance. |
     15	| Node in `Pending` | Longer than 30 minutes: replacement or launch blocked. Check capacity and `LifecycleConfig` logs. |
     16	| Node in `DeepHealthCheckInProgress` | Well past 2 hours. DCGM level 4 alone typically takes about 45 to 90 minutes, and the stress, EFA, and NCCL tests add to it. Check `DeepHealthCheckResults/<id>` streams first |
     17	| `CurrentCount < TargetCount` | Persisting across two inventory reads. |
     18	| `NodeRecovery = None` | Always report. Automatic reboot or replace is disabled. |
     19	| `CurrentImageId != DesiredImageId` | Software update in progress or stalled. |
     20	
     21	## FSx for Lustre (`AWS/FSx`)
     22	
     23	Metric semantics and dimensions:
     24	[FSx for Lustre metrics and dimensions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/fs-metrics.html).
     25

{"id": "577f3ad8-0972-46ba-8cb6-d8e5dc2163a5", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_DltV9MiEr3IBwDxGbCP7GQ", "content": [{"text": "     1	# Frequent Cluster Edge Cases
     2	
     3	Frequent causes of GPU cluster incidents that are not GPU faults. Each has a read-only
     4	detection path and a fixed conclusion. Log strings are quoted from the linked pages.
     5	
     6	## 1. Subnet IP and network interface exhaustion
     7	
     8	Large GPU instances consume many IP addresses, and a subnet's CIDR cannot be changed later.
     9	HyperPod documents that each P5 instance creates **32 IP addresses on Slurm** (one per
     10	network card) and **81 on EKS** (50 from the primary card plus one from each of the other 31).
     11	HyperPod cannot request the ENI quota increase itself.
     12	
     13	Detect:
     14	- `ec2.DescribeSubnets` `AvailableIpAddressCount` for every subnet in `VpcConfig` and each
     15	  group's `OverrideVpcConfig` (HyperPod), or the cluster's compute subnets.
     16	- IPs per node: HyperPod P5 per the figures above; EC2 nodes: count of `NetworkInterfaces`
     17	  plus their secondary private IPs from `DescribeInstances`.
     18	- `servicequotas.GetServiceQuota` for Amazon VPC `L-DF5E4CA3` (Network interfaces per
     19	  Region) versus network interfaces in use.
     20	
     21	Conclude: in an incident, `CurrentCount < TargetCount` with free IPs below one node's need
     22	is a network capacity cause (Branch B), not hardware. In pre-flight, RISK when free IPs
     23	cannot cover one replacement node.
     24	
     25	Source: [HyperPod prerequisites](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-hyperpod-prerequisites.html).
     26	
     27	## 2. EFA security group outbound rule
     28	
     29	HyperPod documents: allow all traffic to and from the security group itself, and "avoid
     30	using `0.0.0.0/0` for outbound rules, as this may cause EFA health check failures". Flag an
     31	outbound `0.0.0.0/0` rule on an EFA HyperPod cluster as RISK, and link it to any EFA deep
     32	health check failure. Source: same page.
     33	
     34	## 3. ParallelCluster nodes that never arrive (scaling, bootstrap, protected mode)
     35	
     36	Streams in `/aws/parallelcluster/<cluster>-<timestamp>` on the head node:
     37	`<host>.<instance-id>.clustermgtd`, `.slurm_resume`, `.slurmctld`; on compute nodes
     38	`.cloud-init-output`.
     39	
     40	| String | Meaning | Conclusion |
     41	|--------|---------|------------|
     42	| `InsufficientInstanceCapacity` in `clustermgtd` or `slurm_resume` | EC2 had no capacity for the launch | Branch B (capacity) |
     43	| `Found the following bootstrap failure nodes` | Nodes launched but failed to join | Configuration or lifecycle failure; node verdict LEAVE ALONE; read the node's `cloud-init-output` |
     44	| `Node bootstrap error` | Reason for a bootstrap failure | Same |
     45	| `Partitions bootstrap failure count` ... `cluster will be set into protected mode if protected failure count reach threshold` | Repeated bootstrap failures | After the threshold, the cluster enters protected mode and stops launching into the failing queue. Report the queue |
     46	
     47	Sources: [Slurm cluster protected mode](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/parallelcluster/latest/ug/slurm-protected-mode-v3.html),
     48	[Node bootstrap error](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/parallelcluster/latest/ug/compute-node-initialization-bootstrap-error-v3.html).
     49	
     50	## 4. EFA nodes in a public subnet (ParallelCluster)
     51	
     52	From ParallelCluster 3.15.0, EFA-enabled nodes launch with more than one network interface,
     53	and "Amazon EC2 does not auto-assign a public IP address to an instance launched with more
     54	than one network interface". Such nodes "fail to bootstrap if they rely on an auto-assigned
     55	public IP for internet access (a public subnet with no NAT gateway)".
     56	
     57	Detect: compute subnet route table has `0.0.0.0/0` to an `igw-` and no NAT; nodes have more
     58	than one network interface and no `PublicIpAddress`. Conclude: proven precondition FAIL,
     59	node verdict LEAVE ALONE. Source: [ParallelCluster EFA](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/parallelcluster/latest/ug/efa-v3.html).
     60	
     61	## 5. Capacity Block not yet active
     62	
     63	`DescribeCapacityReservations` `State = scheduled` with `StartDate` in the future: nodes
     64	cannot launch into it yet. Expected behavior, not a fault. State the start time.
     65	
     66	## 6. FSx for Lustre maintenance window
     67	
     68	`fsx.DescribeFileSystems` `WeeklyMaintenanceStartTime` (day and UTC time). During patching
     69	"your file system will be temporarily unavailable", operations retry, and "the in-memory
     70	cache will be erased during maintenance, leading to higher latencies". A stall that starts
     71	inside the window, followed by higher latency, is FSx maintenance: `Proven` if client I/O
     72	drops exactly in the window, otherwise `Hypothesis`.
     73	Source: [FSx for Lustre maintenance windows](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/maintenance-windows.html).
     74	
     75	## 7. HyperPod-specific visibility
     76	
     77	- HyperPod "currently doesn't support the exportation of system metrics to Amazon
     78	  CloudWatch", and its instances do not appear in the customer account's EC2 APIs. GPU
     79	  activity for HyperPod nodes is therefore `Not observable` in CloudWatch; point to the
     80	  HyperPod observability add-on (Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus). Source:
     81	  [HyperPod FAQ](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-hyperpod-faq-slurm.html).
     82	- Deep health check results are written to `DeepHealthCheckResults/<id>` streams in the
     83	  cluster log group, for example `Encountered FaultyInstance. Replace the Instance. ...
     84	  ERROR:Bandwidth has less than threshold: Expected minimum threshold :80,NCCL Test output Bw: 30`.
     85	  A failure there is hardware-grounded evidence for REPLACE.
     86	- HyperPod EKS node labels (read with the EKS API when available):
     87	  `sagemaker.amazonaws.com/node-health-status` = `Schedulable`, `Unschedulable` (deep
     88	  health checks running), `UnschedulablePendingReplacement`, or `UnschedulablePendingReboot`.
     89	  A node can be `Running` in the SageMaker API while tainted unschedulable. With
     90	  `NodeRecovery = None`, a pending label stays until an operator acts.
     91	  Source: [HyperPod EKS resilience labels](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/sagemaker-hyperpod-eks-resiliency-node-labels.html).
     92	
     93	## 8. Straggler GPU (clock, temperature, power, PCIe)
     94	
     95	With `CWAgent` NVIDIA metrics per `index`: `nvidia_smi_clocks_current_sm`,
     96	`nvidia_smi_temperature_gpu`, `nvidia_smi_power_draw`, `nvidia_smi_pcie_link_width_current`,
     97	`nvidia_smi_pcie_link_gen_current`. One GPU clearly below its peers on the same node during
     98	the same job is a straggler candidate: MONITOR, then REBOOT if it persists. Label it
     99	`Hypothesis` unless it lines up with the slowdown; outlier thresholds are heuristics.
     100	AWS recommends persistently setting maximum clocks
     101	([Optimize GPU settings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/optimize_gpu.html))."}], "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_KwhgRXAIcikEPjRwb4qf7s", "content": [{"text": "     1	# Inventory and Event Timeline
     2	
     3	<!-- Loaded by SKILL.md. Content validated live against HyperPod Slurm, HyperPod EKS, and ParallelCluster clusters. -->
     4	
     5	## Inventory (Step 2): Inventory the cluster
     6	
     7	**HyperPod:**
     8	
     9	```
     10	sagemaker.ListClusters                       # find the cluster if only a name fragment is known
     11	sagemaker.DescribeCluster                    # Orchestrator (Slurm|Eks), NodeRecovery, InstanceGroups
     12	                                             # (InstanceType, CurrentCount, TargetCount,
     13	                                             # OnStartDeepHealthChecks, TrainingPlanArn,
     14	                                             # CurrentImageId vs DesiredImageId), VpcConfig
     15	sagemaker.ListClusterNodes                   # paginate with NextToken until exhausted
     16	sagemaker.DescribeClusterNode                # for every node not in Running, and for any node
     17	                                             # named in the symptom
     18	```
     19	
     20	Record per node: instance ID, instance group, instance type, `InstanceStatus.Status`
     21	(`Running | Failure | Pending | ShuttingDown | SystemUpdating |
     22	DeepHealthCheckInProgress | NotFound`), `InstanceStatus.Message`, launch time, and
     23	private DNS name (the Slurm node name is derived from the private IP).
     24	
     25	Compute per instance group: `CurrentCount` vs `TargetCount`. A persistent shortfall
     26	means nodes are failing to be replaced (branch A or B).
     27	
     28	Record `NodeRecovery`. If it is `None`, HyperPod will not reboot or replace faulty
     29	nodes automatically, and any "auto-resume didn't work" complaint starts there.
     30	
     31	**AWS ParallelCluster or self-managed EC2 or EKS GPU nodes:**
     32	
     33	ParallelCluster nodes carry tags such as `parallelcluster:cluster-name`,
     34	`parallelcluster:node-type` (`HeadNode` or `Compute`), `parallelcluster:queue-name`, and
     35	`parallelcluster:version`. Use them to group compute nodes by cluster and queue, and
     36	keep the head node in scope (it runs `slurmctld` and `clustermgtd`).
     37	
     38	```
     39	ec2.DescribeInstances                        # filter by tag, instance IDs, or instance-type
     40	                                             # p4d.*, p5.*, p5e.*, p5en.*, p6*.*, g5.*, g6*.*
     41	ec2.DescribeInstanceStatus                   # IncludeAllInstances=true; status checks and
     42	                                             # scheduled events
     43	eks.DescribeCluster / eks.ListNodegroups / eks.DescribeNodegroup   # if EKS
     44	```
     45	
     46	**Instance capability profile (every orchestrator, every GPU instance type in the cluster):**
     47	
     48	Do not assume anything from the instance family name. Read it:
     49	
     50	```
     51	ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes                    # for each distinct type; strip the HyperPod "ml."
     52	                                             # prefix (ml.p5.48xlarge -> p5.48xlarge).
     53	                                             # Record GpuInfo.Gpus[].Count and Name,
     54	                                             # NetworkInfo.EfaSupported,
     55	                                             # NetworkInfo.EfaInfo.MaximumEfaInterfaces
     56	ec2.DescribeInstances                        # per node: count NetworkInterfaces with
     57	                                             # InterfaceType efa or efa-only
     58	```
     59	
     60	Derive, per instance type, which checks apply:
     61	
     62	| Property | Source | Checks it turns on |
     63	|----------|--------|--------------------|
     64	| More than one GPU per node | `GpuInfo` count | Intra-node transport (NVLink / P2P vs SHM) |
     65	| `EfaSupported` and more than one node in the job | `NetworkInfo` | Inter-node transport (EFA vs socket fallback), EFA counters, EFA security group |
     66	| EFA interfaces attached per node vs `MaximumEfaInterfaces` | `DescribeInstances` vs `DescribeInstanceTypes` | Fewer attached than the maximum is a RISK: less inter-node bandwidth than the instance supports. Report `<attached> of <max>`. HyperPod nodes run in a SageMaker-managed account, so `DescribeInstances` in the customer account cannot see them: report attached EFA as `Not observable` for HyperPod |
     67	| NVSwitch fabric | `references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md` section 4 (documented families only) | NVLink Xids, Fabric Manager start lines. Unlisted multi-GPU types: `NVSwitch presence unverified`; the operator checks `nvidia-smi topo -m` |
     68	| Software minimums | `references/nccl-nvlink-efa.md` section 5 | Pre-flight P11 |
     69	
     70	**For both:**
     71	
     72	```
     73	ec2.DescribeCapacityReservations             # capacity reservations the nodes run in:
     74	                                             # ReservationType (capacity-block or default),
     75	                                             # State, StartDate, EndDate, TotalInstanceCount,
     76	                                             # AvailableInstanceCount
     77	fsx.DescribeFileSystems                      # Lustre file systems in the cluster VPC:
     78	                                             # DeploymentType, StorageCapacity,
     79	                                             # PerUnitStorageThroughput, Lifecycle
     80	```
     81	
     82	Link each FSx file system to the cluster by VPC and subnet. If none is found, state that
     83	storage was not assessed.
     84	
     85	## Event timeline (Step 3): Build the event timeline
     86	
     87	Pull all of these for the impact window ±30 minutes, then merge them into one ordered
     88	timeline:
     89	
     90	1. **GPU driver (NVRM) messages, from every log source that has them.** The NVIDIA

## Criterion 5 — Capacity reservations
- `DescribeCapacityReservations`: **none** (empty). No Capacity Block or ODCR backing these nodes → these are on-demand dynamic Slurm nodes. No expired/scheduled reservation to explain node loss.

## CWAgent alternative
- `ListMetrics` on `CWAgent`: **no NVIDIA `nvidia_smi_*` metrics** (only `disk_used_percent`/`mem_used_percent` for an unrelated instance i-08a11867e0b7e311d). Finer GPU utilization is NOT available via CWAgent.

## Bottom line for the lead
**The GPUs/compute are not the cause of a throughput drop — because the B200 GPUs were never doing real work during the window.** GPU power never exceeded ~0.6% of max on any node at any time; the two nodes present in-window were idle every hour and terminated ~Sep 27 10:00Z, and no B200 GPU activity was observed for the final ~33h. There are **no hardware fault signals** (StatusCheckFailed = 0, no AWS Health events, no scheduled retirement, no capacity reservation issues).

**Critical cross-branch caveat:** A job running near-zero GPU utilization (or not running at all for large stretches) **cannot have been slowed by FSx for Lustre storage** — an idle/absent job produces no dataset reads. Whatever "throughput drop" was reported is not attributable to GPU/compute hardware, and the FSx storage hypothesis should be re-examined against *when a job was actually running* (the real training burst was on **Sep 23**, before this window). 

**Open items (not owned by me / not observable):** (1) EFA attached-vs-max is unverifiable with all nodes terminated — recommend re-checking on a live node (RISK: could be <8 of 8). (2) Confirming whether a job was scheduled/running at all in the window belongs to Slurm/scheduler + deployment branches.

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### B200 training throughput dropped over the last few days
**Description:** Training throughput on the B200 ParallelCluster `distributed-training-triage-b200` degraded noticeably over the last few days while reading its dataset from FSx for Lustre `fs-077c776983688ad76`. Open question: is storage (FSx Lustre), network (EFA/NCCL), or the GPUs responsible?
**Time:** 2026-09-25T16:00:00Z

## Findings

### Cause: Compute launches failing: Capacity Reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b not active
**Description:** Slurm on the head node (i-01bbde10b04dd4ca8) issues RunInstances for p6-b200.48xlarge compute nodes that FAIL roughly every minute with `Client.InvalidParameterValue: Capacity Reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is not active.` The CR cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b no longer exists (DescribeCapacityReservations returns InvalidCapacityReservationId.NotFound). Net effect: no B200 compute nodes can launch, so training is effectively halted. Onset ~2026-09-27 (failure storm observed 11:07-11:19Z) after a fresh head-node start (head-node role credentials issued 2026-09-27T06:35:58Z); no RunInstances before 2026-09-25.
**Cascades to:** symptom-b200-throughput

### Root Cause: Launch template repointed to a now-dead Capacity Block
**Description:** A CloudFormation UpdateStack on 2026-09-22 19:33Z (by Admin/sureshnt-Isengard) created launch template lt-025a88cbeaba7b869 v2, repointing the p6-b200.48xlarge compute queue's CapacityReservationTarget from the original Capacity Block cr-0884d02f8b1b344e5 (v1) to cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b (carried through v3 and v4). cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is now inactive/NotFound. Slurm launches against the latest LT version (v4), so every RunInstances fails with 'Capacity Reservation cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b is not active'; no B200 nodes have existed since ~2026-09-27T10:00Z. Both prior Capacity Blocks (cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b and cr-0884d02f8b1b344e5) are now NotFound and no active p6-b200.48xlarge reservation exists — a config rollback would only restore a dead reference, so a new Capacity Block for ML must be acquired. This is the fundamental cause the throughput collapse cascades from.
**Cascades to:** finding-capacity-reservation

### Hypothesis: FSx storage saturation
**Description:** Originally flagged as a SCRATCH_2 network-throughput bottleneck based on an hourly-resolution reading that appeared to peak at 124.73%. That was a distill misread of the hourly data. Verified 5-minute-resolution metrics show the file system is essentially idle: network/disk/IOPS utilization stayed ≤0.13% and MDS CPU ≤7.57% — roughly 2000x below saturation. Baseline reads ~20KB/hour with only four brief isolated bursts (largest ~19.7 MB/s averaged over an hour, vs the ~240 MB/s SCRATCH_2 baseline). No fill-up, no metadata pressure, no maintenance-window correlation.
**Cascades to:** symptom-b200-throughput

#### Supporting Observations
- **FSx is a small SCRATCH_2 filesystem (1.2 TiB, ~240 MB/s baseline):** `fs-077c776983688ad76` is FSx for Lustre SCRATCH_2, 1200 GiB SSD, AVAILABLE, DataCompression NONE, logging DISABLED. SCRATCH_2 delivers ~200 MB/s per TiB, so 1.2 TiB implies only ~240 MB/s of aggregate baseline throughput — very small for a B200 job, making a storage throughput bottleneck a strong hypothesis to test.

#### Gaps
- **Observability gap: kernel/NCCL/Lustre signals not shipped:** The /aws/fsx-training/distributed-training-triage-b200/kernel pipeline ships no kernel: lines and compute-node streams went silent after 2026-09-27 11:00Z; job stdout and NCCL debug are not shipped. So GPU Xids, Lustre client errors, and NCCL transport are all NOT OBSERVABLE. Fix CloudWatch-agent log config, enable NCCL debug, ship job stdout for future triage.
- **Why GPUs were idle Sep 25–27 while nodes were up:** During the one window nodes ran (Sep 25 19:00–Sep 27 10:00Z) GPUs stayed ≤0.58% power with negligible FSx reads and zero writes — no productive job. Not determinable from remote telemetry (job stdout not shipped, Slurm control-plane streams stale). Operator should check on-node: sacct, job logs.

### Hypothesis: Network/EFA fabric as cause
**Description:** Checked the compute queue EFA configuration (launch template lt-025a88cbeaba7b869, 8 efa-only NICs per node), compute-node security-group membership (members of FSx SG sg-0c6c57aa6bccdbb0d), subnet placement (same subnet-024dbe437aef9d7eb as FSx, same AZ), and routing (private subnet with a NAT path). One benign risk noted: compute SG sg-085312d23331273ac egress lacks an explicit self-reference but is covered by 0.0.0.0/0 today.

- **Why GPUs were idle Sep 25–27 while nodes were up:** During the one window nodes ran (Sep 25 19:00–Sep 27 10:00Z) GPUs stayed ≤0.58% power with negligible FSx reads and zero writes — no productive job. # Mitigation Summary

## Action
Acquire a new Capacity Block for ML and repoint the distributed-training-triage-b200 compute queue at its reservation via pcluster update-cluster, so p6-b200.48xlarge nodes can launch again.

## Reasoning
The B200 compute queue (launch template lt-025a88cbeaba7b869) uses the Capacity Block for ML model (MarketType: capacity-block). Both Capacity Blocks it has pinned are gone: latest versions v2-v4 target cr-0013d27d3b3d5dc3b (NotFound) and v1 targeted cr-0884d02f8b1b344e5 (also NotFound). No valid p6-b200.48xlarge reservation exists, so a launch-template / CloudFormation rollback would not help - a new Capacity Block must be purchased and the queue repointed at it. Training cannot resume until a valid CB is active; the available offering cb-08f51ed0da4ac0bde starts 2026-09-30T11:30Z.

## Execution Plan

### Step 1: Pre Validate

#### 1.1 Confirm no active or inactive p6-b200.48xlarge reservation remains to…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-capacity-reservations --filters Name=instance-type,Values=p6-b200.48xlarge --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Confirm no active or inactive p6-b200.48xlarge reservation remains to repoint at.

#### 1.2 Locate a purchasable Capacity Block offering for the B200 queue
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-capacity-block-offerings --instance-type p6-b200.48xlarge --instance-count 2 --capacity-duration-hours 24 --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Locate a purchasable Capacity Block offering for the B200 queue.

### Step 2: Apply

#### 2.1 Purchase the new Capacity Block to obtain a valid p6-b200.48xlarge…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 purchase-capacity-block --capacity-block-offering-id cb-08f51ed0da4ac0bde --instance-platform Linux/UNIX --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Purchase the new Capacity Block to obtain a valid p6-b200.48xlarge reservation.
**Risks:** Upfront fee of $4,744.32, Capacity is active only 2026-09-30T11:30Z -> 2026-10-01T11:30Z

#### 2.2 Point the B200 compute resource at the newly purchased reservation id
**Type:** command
```
# In the ParallelCluster cluster config, set the B200 compute resource:
Scheduling:
  SlurmQueues:
    - Name: gpu
      ComputeResources:
        - Name: p6b20048xlarge
          InstanceType: p6-b200.48xlarge
          CapacityReservationTarget:
            CapacityReservationId: <NEW_RESERVATION_ID>  # from purchase-capacity-block output
```
**Purpose:** Point the B200 compute resource at the newly purchased reservation id.

#### 2.3 Repoint the B200 compute queue at the valid reservation so Slurm can…
**Type:** command
```
pcluster update-cluster --cluster-name distributed-training-triage-b200 --cluster-configuration updated-config.yaml --region us-west-2
```
**Purpose:** Repoint the B200 compute queue at the valid reservation so Slurm can launch nodes.
**Risks:** Requires the compute fleet stopped / queue idle for the update, Training cannot start before the Capacity Block start time (2026-09-30T11:30Z)

### Step 3: Post Validate

#### 3.1 Confirm p6-b200.48xlarge compute nodes now launch and reach Running…
**Type:** command
```
aws ec2 describe-instances --filters Name=tag:parallelcluster:cluster-name,Values=distributed-training-triage-b200 Name=tag:parallelcluster:node-type,Values=Compute --region us-west-2 --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].{Id:InstanceId,State:State.Name}'
```
**Purpose:** Confirm p6-b200.48xlarge compute nodes now launch and reach Running (RunInstances no longer errors on the dead reservation).

#### 3.2 Confirm GPUs pick up real training work after nodes launch
**Type:** text
Once a job runs, confirm GPUPowerUtilization climbs well above the ~0.5% idle floor observed during the incident, indicating GPUs are doing real work.
**Purpose:** Confirm GPUs pick up real training work after nodes launch.

#### 3.3 Restore kernel-log shipping so Xid/NCCL/Lustre signals are observable…
**Type:** text
Fix the CloudWatch agent kernel-log shipping for /aws/fsx-training/distributed-training-triage-b200/kernel so kernel:/NVRM: Xid, Lustre client, and NCCL transport lines reach CloudWatch again (they stopped after 2026-09-24 19:29Z, leaving the last ~32h uncovered).
**Purpose:** Restore kernel-log shipping so Xid/NCCL/Lustre signals are observable in future incidents.
**Advisory:** Does not affect the immediate fix; improves future triage coverage

ENVIRONMENT: AWS account 111122223333, region us-west-2. FSx: fs-077c776983688ad76, LUSTRE, DeploymentType SCRATCH_2, StorageType SSD, StorageCapacity 1200 GiB (~1.17 TiB). SCRATCH_2 baseline network throughput is ~200 MB/s per TiB, so this file system's baseline aggregate is only ~240 MB/s — small for a B200 job. WeeklyMaintenanceStartTime is "4:11:30" (Thursday 11:30 UTC).

TASK:
1. First run cloudwatch.ListMetrics for namespace AWS/FSx filtered to FileSystemId=fs-077c776983688ad76 to DISCOVER the real dimension values — the FileServer values (including any metadata-server "MDS*" value) and the StorageTargetId (OST) values. Do NOT guess them.
2. Then pull these AWS/FSx metrics with cloudwatch.GetMetricData. Use two passes: (a) a 7-day trend window 2026-09-21T00:00:00Z → 2026-09-28T19:40:00Z at 1-hour period to see the onset and a healthy baseline; (b) a zoom on the last 72 hours 2026-09-25T19:00:00Z → 2026-09-28T19:40:00Z at 5-minute period.
   - DataReadBytes, DataWriteBytes, MetadataOperations, ClientConnections — dimension FileSystemId only, stat Sum. Convert byte Sums to a rate: MB/s = Sum / period_seconds / 1e6. Do NOT report raw Sum as a rate.
   - NetworkThroughputUtilization, FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization — dimensions FileSystemId + FileServer, stat Maximum.
   - DiskIopsUtilization — dimensions FileSystemId + StorageTargetId, stat Maximum (NOTE: often not published on SCRATCH_2; if absent, report it as not published for this deployment type, do NOT read absent as zero).
   - CPUUtilization for the metadata server — dimensions FileSystemId + FileServer (the MDS* value), stat Maximum.
   - FreeDataStorageCapacity — dimensions FileSystemId + StorageTargetId, stat Minimum per OST and Sum overall.

ANALYSIS CRITERIA (ranked):
1. Is NetworkThroughputUtilization or FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization at/near saturation (≥90% sustained 5+ min, and how close to 100%) during the slow period? These utilization metrics are already a percent from 0–100 — a value of 0.9 means 0.9%, quote the raw value with a % sign.
2. TREND: over the 7-day window, did utilization rise, did FreeDataStorageCapacity fall (SCRATCH fills up), or did MetadataOperations climb over the last few days? Pin the approximate time the change began.
3. Classify: throughput-bound (large sequential reads/writes saturating network or disk throughput) vs metadata-bound (high MetadataOperations, MDS CPUUtilization high, throughput well below capacity). The fix differs, so state which the metrics show.
4. FreeDataStorageCapacity: any single OST near full (<10% free) while others have space → imbalanced striping.
5. Correlate DataReadBytes/DataWriteBytes: a drop in client I/O is usually the EFFECT of a stall unless a saturation metric rose FIRST. State which case applies.
6. FSx maintenance window: does any I/O drop start exactly inside Thursday 11:30 UTC?

Per the skill (branch C): if no FSx metric is near saturation, state storage is NOT saturated and do not recommend raising throughput. FSx does not publish client-side latency, so a metadata/IO spike without a saturated metric makes FSx a "Hypothesis (to validate)", not a proven cause; a saturated throughput metric during the slow period is a "Proven" cause. Label your conclusion accordingly.

EXCLUSIONS: Do NOT investigate GPUs, EFA/NCCL, security groups, or CloudTrail — other subagents own those. Report only FSx storage findings with concrete numbers, timestamps, and the exact metric/dimension each rests on.", "type": "text"}], "user_reference": null}

{"id": "d610ce36-86f2-4189-861a-3c8c7b4300bb", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "63451c1b-070a-45b5-891e-2233732c918b", "content": [{"text": "Successfully loaded /aidevops/skills/system/exploring-metrics/SKILL.md"}], "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "9d4b9566-42b4-4ba4-9007-f00fd0ab384c", "content": [{"text": "     1	---
     2	name: aiml-gpu-training-cluster-investigation
     3	description: Use this skill for GPU training or inference clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or
     4	  EKS), ParallelCluster, or self-managed EC2/EKS GPU instances. It adds three things.
     5	  First, a GPU evidence coverage audit that proves per node whether kernel Xid logs and
     6	  HyperPod health-agent detections were actually arriving, hour by hour, so "no errors
     7	  found" is never reported from a silent log. Second, a node verdict (replace, reboot,
     8	  or leave alone) against an explicit evidence bar, so an application Xid is never
     9	  headlined as hardware. Third, a pre-flight readiness check before a long run, covering
     10	  Capacity Block or training plan end time versus run length, spare capacity to replace
     11	  a failed node, NodeRecovery, deep health checks, EFA, log coverage, idle reserved
     12	  GPUs. Activate on Xid or ECC errors, slow training or FSx for Lustre slowness on a GPU
     13	  cluster, NCCL hangs or TCP fallback, NVLink or Fabric Manager errors, nodes in Failure
     14	  or Pending, nodes terminating at once, or "is my cluster ready for a multi-day run".
     15	metadata:
     16	  author: nzuresh
     17	  version: "1.0.0"
     18	  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: "Incident RCA, Chat tasks"
     19	  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: "Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, AWS ParallelCluster, Amazon EC2, Amazon FSx for Lustre, Elastic Fabric Adapter, Amazon EKS, AWS Health"
     20	  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: "Machine Learning, GenAI, High Performance Computing"
     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass.** In chat, do not stop to ask a question and do not hand off to a
     34	   separate investigation before answering. If an input is missing, use the default (impact
     35	   window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and 72 hours), state the assumption,
     36	   and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or performance questions with no
     37	   time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only after the answer.
     38	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     39	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     40	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     41	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     42	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     43	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     44	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     45	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     46	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     47	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     48	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     49	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     50	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     51	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     52	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     53	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     54	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     55	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     56	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.
     57	R4. **Find every log source by substring, not prefix.** Call `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with
     58	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for
     59	   `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`, `journal`, and `gpu`, paginating with `nextToken`. Never
     60	   search only `/aws/parallelcluster` or `/aws/sagemaker` prefixes: customer pipelines use
     61	   other names (for example `/aws/<pipeline>/<cluster>/kernel`). Evaluate every source found.
     62	R5. **Prove coverage before any "no errors".** For each node and source: find the stream that
     63	   carries `kernel:` lines, then bin **that exact stream** by hour across the window padded by
     64	   one hour. **Always name the evidence you used: quote the full log group name and the exact
     65	   log stream name for every node in the coverage table, and again in the answer text.** A
     66	   coverage claim without the group and stream it rests on is not auditable, so the operator
     67	   cannot re-run it. Any empty hour means `Not observable` for that hour. First and last event times
     68	   are not proof, and the time of the **last `kernel:` line** is not when logging stopped:
     69	   a healthy kernel goes quiet. Liveness comes only from the hourly bins of all lines in
     70	   that stream. A node is `Measured` if one source passes. HyperPod: a missing
     71	   `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<group>/<instance-id>` stream means `No HMA detections`
     72	   when the cluster log group is otherwise live. NCCL transport with no `NCCL INFO` lines
     73	   anywhere is `Not observable`; never infer it from the instance type.
     74	R6. **Verdict per node, headline to match.** `REPLACE`, `REBOOT`, `LEAVE ALONE`, `MONITOR`, or
     75	   `NOT OBSERVABLE`, against the evidence bar in `references/incident-branches.md` (Step 4b).
     76	   Application-class Xids (for example 13, 31) or HMA `reason: XidUserAppError` with the node
     77	   `Running` is `LEAVE ALONE`. Never headline "hardware error" unless the verdict is `REPLACE`
     78	   or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds.
     79	R7. **Label every cause** `Proven` (measured signal on the affected node, before the failure,
     80	   nothing competing) or `Hypothesis (to validate)` with the one confirming measurement. A
     81	   spike at the same time is correlation. FSx without a saturated metric is not a proven cause.
     82	   Only a `Proven` cause may be called the root cause, in the headline or in a branch table.
     83	   Otherwise write `Leading hypothesis: <cause>`, or `Root cause: Not observable` when the
     84	   deciding evidence is missing (for example a dead control-plane log). Never write "Proven
     85	   mechanism" for something whose trigger or removal path you did not observe.
     86	   Utilization metrics from FSx (`NetworkThroughputUtilization`, `DiskIopsUtilization`, and
     87	   similar) and `GPUPowerUtilization` are already percent from 0 to 100: a value of `0.9` is
     88	   0.9 percent. Quote the raw value with a percent sign.
     89	R8. **Recovery questions** always state three things: whether automatic node recovery is on
     90	   (`NodeRecovery`), what it does (reboot or replace the node), and that the **job** resumes
     91	   only with checkpoints plus the orchestrator's auto-resume (Slurm on HyperPod:
     92	   `srun --auto-resume=1`).
     93	R9. **Capacity Blocks** begin terminating instances 30 minutes before the end time (60 for
     94	   UltraServers); blocks end at 11:30 UTC and termination starts at 11:00 UTC on the last day.
     95	   For a planned run, write out: usable until = end time minus the lead time; run end = start
     96	   plus run length; hours covered = usable until minus start. Give every value as a full UTC
     97	   date and time, and check the latest safe start is not already in the past.
     98	R10. **Rule out the frequent non-GPU causes** in `references/cluster-edge-cases.md` before
     99	   blaming hardware: subnet IP or network interface exhaustion, ParallelCluster bootstrap
     100	   failures and protected mode, EFA nodes in a public subnet, a Capacity Block not yet
     101	   active, and the FSx maintenance window. HyperPod does not export system metrics to
     102	   CloudWatch, so HyperPod GPU activity is `Not observable` there.
     103

     105

     112	## Workflow checklist

     184	Pull FSx (correct dimensions per metric), GPU activity (`AWS/EC2` `GPUPowerUtilization`, unit

{"id": "c840fbed-efa8-4ee1-8c22-38cb151d431b", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_0uGtyVsI8PmsA2FQtDBdwF", "content": [{"text": "     1	# Signals and Thresholds
     2	
     3	Thresholds here are investigation heuristics for flagging a signal as worth reporting.
     4	They are not AWS service limits. State the observed value, not only the label.
     5	
     6	## HyperPod node state
     7	
     8	Valid `InstanceStatus.Status` values
     9	([ClusterInstanceStatusDetails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_ClusterInstanceStatusDetails.html)):
     10	`Running | Failure | Pending | ShuttingDown | SystemUpdating | DeepHealthCheckInProgress | NotFound`.
     11	
     12	| Signal | Flag when |
     13	|--------|-----------|
     14	| Node in `Failure` | Always. Correlate with HMA log for that instance. |
     15	| Node in `Pending` | Longer than 30 minutes: replacement or launch blocked. Check capacity and `LifecycleConfig` logs. |
     16	| Node in `DeepHealthCheckInProgress` | Well past 2 hours. DCGM level 4 alone typically takes about 45 to 90 minutes, and the stress, EFA, and NCCL tests add to it. Check `DeepHealthCheckResults/<id>` streams first |
     17	| `CurrentCount < TargetCount` | Persisting across two inventory reads. |
     18	| `NodeRecovery = None` | Always report. Automatic reboot or replace is disabled. |
     19	| `CurrentImageId != DesiredImageId` | Software update in progress or stalled. |
     20	
     21	## FSx for Lustre (`AWS/FSx`)
     22	
     23	Metric semantics and dimensions:
     24	[FSx for Lustre metrics and dimensions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/fs-metrics.html).
     25	
     26	| Metric (dimensions) | Stat | Flag when | Meaning |
     27	|---------------------|------|-----------|---------|
     28	| `NetworkThroughputUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | File server network throughput saturated |
     29	| `FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | OSS-to-disk throughput saturated |
     30	| `DiskIopsUtilization` (FileSystemId, StorageTargetId) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | OST IOPS saturated (not on Scratch or Persistent HDD) |
     31	| `CPUUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer = MDS*) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | Metadata server saturated |
     32	| `MetadataOperations` (FileSystemId) | Sum / period | Sharp rise aligned with the slowdown | Metadata-heavy workload |
     33	| `FreeDataStorageCapacity` (FileSystemId, StorageTargetId) | Minimum per OST | Any OST < 10% free while others have space | Imbalanced striping, write failures possible |
     34	| `DataReadBytes` + `DataWriteBytes` (FileSystemId) | Sum / period | Drop aligned with the stall | Clients stopped doing I/O (effect, not cause) |
     35

     2	
     3	Thresholds here are investigation heuristics for flagging a signal as worth reporting.
     4	They are not AWS service limits. State the observed value, not only the label.
     5	
     6	## HyperPod node state
     7	
     8	Valid `InstanceStatus.Status` values
     9	([ClusterInstanceStatusDetails](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/APIReference/API_ClusterInstanceStatusDetails.html)):
     10	`Running | Failure | Pending | ShuttingDown | SystemUpdating | DeepHealthCheckInProgress | NotFound`.
     11	
     12	| Signal | Flag when |
     13	|--------|-----------|
     14	| Node in `Failure` | Always. Correlate with HMA log for that instance. |
     15	| Node in `Pending` | Longer than 30 minutes: replacement or launch blocked. Check capacity and `LifecycleConfig` logs. |
     16	| Node in `DeepHealthCheckInProgress` | Well past 2 hours. DCGM level 4 alone typically takes about 45 to 90 minutes, and the stress, EFA, and NCCL tests add to it. Check `DeepHealthCheckResults/<id>` streams first |
     17	| `CurrentCount < TargetCount` | Persisting across two inventory reads. |
     18	| `NodeRecovery = None` | Always report. Automatic reboot or replace is disabled. |
     19	| `CurrentImageId != DesiredImageId` | Software update in progress or stalled. |
     20	
     21	## FSx for Lustre (`AWS/FSx`)
     22	
     23	Metric semantics and dimensions:
     24	[FSx for Lustre metrics and dimensions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/fs-metrics.html).
     25	
     26	| Metric (dimensions) | Stat | Flag when | Meaning |
     27	|---------------------|------|-----------|---------|
     28	| `NetworkThroughputUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | File server network throughput saturated |
     29	| `FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | OSS-to-disk throughput saturated |
     30	| `DiskIopsUtilization` (FileSystemId, StorageTargetId) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | OST IOPS saturated (not on Scratch or Persistent HDD) |
     31	| `CPUUtilization` (FileSystemId, FileServer = MDS*) | Maximum | ≥ 90% sustained 5+ min | Metadata server saturated |
     32	| `MetadataOperations` (FileSystemId) | Sum / period | Sharp rise aligned with the slowdown | Metadata-heavy workload |
     33	| `FreeDataStorageCapacity` (FileSystemId, StorageTargetId) | Minimum per OST | Any OST < 10% free while others have space | Imbalanced striping, write failures possible |
     34	| `DataReadBytes` + `DataWriteBytes` (FileSystemId) | Sum / period | Drop aligned with the stall | Clients stopped doing I/O (effect, not cause) |
     35	
     36	Throughput in bytes per second is `Sum / period_seconds`. Do not report raw `Sum` as a
     37	rate.
     38	
     39	A drop in client I/O during a hang is usually the **effect** of the job stalling. It
     40	points at storage only if a saturation metric above rose first.

     43	
     44	`AWS/EC2` `GPUPowerUtilization` (dimensions `InstanceId` and `GpuId`, as observed in live
     45	accounts; the EC2 docs list the metric but not the `GpuId` dimension) is published by EC2 for a
     46	subset of accelerated instance types without an agent. Unit is Percent of maximum active

     15	metadata:

     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass.** In chat, do not stop to ask a question and do not hand off to a
     34	   separate investigation before answering. If an input is missing, use the default (impact
     35	   window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and 72 hours), state the assumption,
     36	   and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or performance questions with no
     37	   time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only after the answer.
     38	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     39	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     40	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     41	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     42	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     43	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     44	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     45	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     46	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     47	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     48	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     49	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     50	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     51	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     52	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     53	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     54	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     55	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     56	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.
     57	R4. **Find every log source by substring, not prefix.** Call `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with
     58	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for
     59	   `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`, `journal`, and `gpu`, paginating with `nextToken`. Never
     60	   search only `/aws/parallelcluster` or `/aws/sagemaker` prefixes: customer pipelines use
     61	   other names (for example `/aws/<pipeline>/<cluster>/kernel`). Evaluate every source found.
     62	R5. **Prove coverage before any "no errors".** For each node and source: find the stream that
     63	   carries `kernel:` lines, then bin **that exact stream** by hour across the window padded by
     64	   one hour. **Always name the evidence you used: quote the full log group name and the exact
     65	   log stream name for every node in the coverage table, and again in the answer text.** A
     66	   coverage claim without the group and stream it rests on is not auditable, so the operator
     67	   cannot re-run it. Any empty hour means `Not observable` for that hour. First and last event times
     68	   are not proof, and the time of the **last `kernel:` line** is not when logging stopped:
     69	   a healthy kernel goes quiet. Liveness comes only from the hourly bins of all lines in
     70	   that stream. A node is `Measured` if one source passes. HyperPod: a missing
     71	   `SagemakerHealthMonitoringAgent/<group>/<instance-id>` stream means `No HMA detections`
     72	   when the cluster log group is otherwise live. NCCL transport with no `NCCL INFO` lines
     73	   anywhere is `Not observable`; never infer it from the instance type.
     74	R6. **Verdict per node, headline to match.** `REPLACE`, `REBOOT`, `LEAVE ALONE`, `MONITOR`, or
     75	   `NOT OBSERVABLE`, against the evidence bar in `references/incident-branches.md` (Step 4b).
     76	   Application-class Xids (for example 13, 31) or HMA `reason: XidUserAppError` with the node
     77	   `Running` is `LEAVE ALONE`. Never headline "hardware error" unless the verdict is `REPLACE`
     78	   or `REBOOT` on hardware grounds.
     79	R7. **Label every cause** `Proven` (measured signal on the affected node, before the failure,
     80	   nothing competing) or `Hypothesis (to validate)` with the one confirming measurement. A
     81	   spike at the same time is correlation. FSx without a saturated metric is not a proven cause.
     82	   Only a `Proven` cause may be called the root cause, in the headline or in a branch table.
     83	   Otherwise write `Leading hypothesis: <cause>`, or `Root cause: Not observable` when the

     3	Where each GPU-communication signal can be seen, what a good and a bad value look like,

     7	## 1. Which transport NCCL actually used
     8	
     9	NCCL writes its transport choices only when `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` (or higher) is set, and only
     10	to the job's stdout or to `NCCL_DEBUG_FILE`. These reach CloudWatch only if the customer
     11	ships job output. Search every log source found in SKILL.md Step 3a for `NCCL INFO` and
     12	`NCCL WARN` first. **If there are no NCCL lines at all, NCCL transport is `Not observable`.**
     13	Never infer "NCCL used EFA" from the instance type or the EFA security group.
     14	
     15	| Log line | Meaning | Verdict |
     16	|----------|---------|---------|
     17	| `NET/OFI Selected Provider is efa` and `Using network AWS Libfabric` | Inter-node traffic goes over EFA through the AWS OFI NCCL plugin | Good |
     18	| `Using network IB` | NCCL chose an InfiniBand-verbs network | Unexpected on EC2 EFA instances; report it |
     19	| Channel lines `... via NET/Socket/<n>` | Inter-node traffic over TCP sockets | **Bad** on EFA instances: silent fallback. The AWS blog on P3dn measured about a three-fold bus-bandwidth gain for EFA over TCP |
     20	| Channel lines `... via P2P/CUMEM` | Intra-node GPU to GPU by direct peer access (NVLink on NVSwitch nodes) | Good |
     21	| `NVLS Creating Multicast group ...` | NVLink SHARP in use for collectives | Good on NVSwitch systems that support it |
     22	| Channel lines `... via SHM/direct/direct` | Intra-node traffic through host shared memory | On an NVSwitch node, peer access is not being used; report as degraded |
     23	
     24	Sources: [NCCL logging](https://docs.nvidia.com/deeplearning/nccl/user-guide/docs/troubleshooting/logging.html),
     25	[Training LLMs on SageMaker: best practices](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/machine-learning/training-large-language-models-on-amazon-sagemaker-best-practices/),
     26	[Optimizing deep learning on P3dn with EFA](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/optimizing-deep-learning-on-p3-and-p3dn-with-efa/).
     27	
     28	When NCCL is not observable, give the operator this to collect on one affected job:
     29	`NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,NET,P2P,SHM,NVLS NCCL_DEBUG_FILE=/fsx/nccl_%h_%p.log`
     30	(subsystem names from the NCCL logging page), then search the files for the lines above.
     31	
     32	## 2. NVLink and NVSwitch fabric
     33	
     34	The CloudWatch agent's NVIDIA plugin does **not** collect any NVLink counter (its full
     35	metric list is utilization, temperature, power, memory, PCIe link, encoder, and clocks).
     36	NVLink health reaches AWS only through the system log:
     37	
     38	| Signal | Where | Meaning |
     39	|--------|-------|---------|
     40	| `NVRM: Xid ...: 74` | Kernel log, HyperPod HMA | NVLink error (NVIDIA catalog: immediate action per NVLink workflow, investigatory action contact support). Hardware class |
     41	| `NVRM: Xid ...: 71`, `NVLink: fatal error detected on link <n>` | Kernel log, HyperPod HMA (`reason: XidHardwareFailure`) | Fatal NVLink error; example in the HyperPod HMA documentation. Hardware class |

Hardware or driver-stack problem: node verdict `REBOOT`, then `REPLACE` if it recurs. AWS documents Fabric Manager as required on P6-B200 and P6-B300; on other NVSwitch types, report a failure as a strong signal but label the NVLink impact `Hypothesis (to validate)` with `nvidia-smi topo -m` as the check |

     21	---
     22	
     23	# GPU Cluster Evidence, Readiness, and Fault Verdicts
     24	
     25	For GPU clusters on SageMaker HyperPod (Slurm or EKS), AWS ParallelCluster, and self-managed
     26	EC2 or EKS. Generic investigation finds the obvious signals; this skill adds what it gets
     27	wrong: silent evidence, wrong-headline hardware verdicts, and predictable failures before a
     28	long run. **Read-only.** Never reboot, replace, update, or delete anything, and never read
     29	training data, checkpoints, or model weights.
     30	
     31	## Critical rules R1 to R10 (apply in every mode, in this order)
     32	
     33	R1. **Answer in one pass.** In chat, do not stop to ask a question and do not hand off to a
     34	   separate investigation before answering. If an input is missing, use the default (impact
     35	   window: last 24 hours; run length: evaluate 24, 48, and 72 hours), state the assumption,
     36	   and mark dependent checks `Needs input`. For "slow" or performance questions with no
     37	   time given, use the last 72 hours. Offer follow-ups only after the answer.
     38	R2. **Inventory and capability profile.** HyperPod: `sagemaker.DescribeCluster` and
     39	   `ListClusterNodes` (paginate). EC2/ParallelCluster/EKS: `ec2.DescribeInstances`. For every
     40	   GPU instance type: `ec2.DescribeInstanceTypes` (strip HyperPod `ml.`): GPU count,
     41	   `EfaSupported`, `MaximumEfaInterfaces`; per EC2 node, attached `efa`/`efa-only` interfaces.
     42	   Report `<attached> of <max>`, where attached = interfaces with `InterfaceType` `efa` or
     43	   `efa-only` (the primary ENA interface does not count unless it is `efa`). HyperPod nodes
     44	   are not visible to `DescribeInstances`: say so. On NVSwitch types, search every log source
     45	   found under rule R4 for `Started "Nvidia Fabric Manager"` before saying it is not confirmed.
     46	R3. **Node identity survives replacement.** A HyperPod reboot keeps the instance ID; a replace
     47	   gives the node a **new instance ID in the same instance group**, so the current ID will
     48	   never appear in the replace request. Query CloudTrail **by event name, not by instance
     49	   ID**: `cloudtrail.LookupEvents` with `LookupAttributes=[{AttributeKey: EventName,
     50	   AttributeValue: BatchReplaceClusterNodes}]`, then again for `BatchRebootClusterNodes`,
     51	   `BatchDeleteClusterNodes`, and `UpdateCluster`, with `StartTime` = window start minus 6
     52	   hours and `EndTime` = now as full ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, paginating with `NextToken`.
     53	   Keep events whose `requestParameters.clusterName` is this cluster. A `nodeIds` entry
     54	   that is not in the current `ListClusterNodes` output was replaced; the instance group
     55	   whose node has a `LaunchTime` just after that event is the replaced group. That operator
     56	   or automatic call is the explanation for the node going `Pending` (Branch E), not hardware.
     57	R4. **Find every log source by substring, not prefix.** Call `logs.DescribeLogGroups` with
     58	   `logGroupNamePattern` (case-sensitive substring) = the cluster name, then again for
     59	   `kernel`, `messages`, `syslog`, `journal`, and `gpu`, paginating with `nextToken`. Never
